proposed.text: An architect assigned all copyright in a building design to a developer. The developer then licensed the design to a competitor without the architect's permission. What rights does the architect have?

options.text: The architect retains economic copyright rights and can sue for ordinary licensing infringement despite the full assignment
The architect retains personal moral rights such as attribution and integrity, but not the assigned economic copyright rights
The architect has no remaining rights of any kind after assignment
The architect retains moral rights only if the assignment agreement repeats them

rationale.a: After a full economic assignment, the architect no longer controls the assigned economic licensing rights unless the agreement limits the assignment.
rationale.c: This ignores moral rights under Sections 193 and 198.
rationale.d: Moral rights arise from statute, not only from contract reservation.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180 allows copyright assignment and gives the assignee the assigned rights and remedies. Sections 193 and 198 preserve the author's moral rights and make those rights non-assignable and not subject to license. Section 195 allows limited written waiver, but assignment of economic copyright does not assign moral rights.
rationale.takeaway: Economic rights can be assigned; moral rights remain personal to the author.
